title: Edge-to-core serving model selection - draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note from the 2024-11-08 solutions workshop with the retail customer (internal alias: OrbitMall). The goal: propose a concise set of architecture patterns that balance 1) sub-100ms inference for interactive checkout flows, 2) predictable monthly costs, and 3) data sovereignty for EU users. This file is intentionally informal — use for quick handoffs and to capture open questions and next steps.

Context / constraints (customer):
- Target flows: product Q&A widget (token-limited prompts), purchase assistant chat, and lightweight reranking for search suggestions.
- Peak qps: expected 600 requests/s (spikey during holiday windows). Baseline 24h p95 latency requirement: < 120ms for widget median; critical checkout paths require < 100ms 99th at peak.
- Data: product catalog + user session metadata (PII blocked). EU data residency required for EU customers.
- Procurement: short pilot (3 months), then likely committed Dedicated or Private for PCI-adjacent features.
- Budget signal: customer prefers predictable committed spend vs volatile per-token costs.

Candidate architecture patterns (3 high-level options):
1) Centralized Hosted (single-hosted region per geography)
   - Model variant: fp16 optimized open Llama-2-70B-mix (quantized for cost).
   - Traffic shape: region-based routing -> single hosted cluster per region.
   - Pros: fastest to stand up; no infra ops for customer; automatic autoscaling. Good for immediate pilot.
   - Cons: burst cold starts during holiday spiky traffic; egress costs if using cross-region fallbacks; less control for strict SLA guarantees.
   - SLO mapping: p50/p95 likely fine; p99 where customer cares may need fallbacks to smaller model or pre-warmed warm-pools.

2) Hybrid Dedicated Pools + Hosted Fallback (recommended for pilot-to-prod path)
   - Pattern: Dedicated GPU pool reserved for critical routes (checkout/chat). Non-critical and overflow routed to hosted. Canary routing for model upgrades.
   - Model variants: dedicate 1x 8-GPU A100 pool running quantized int8 variant for the critical path; hosted uses larger model or same model in lower-cost configuration.
   - Pros: predictable throughput for critical lanes; cost efficiency via committed capacity; graceful degradation path to hosted if dedicated saturated.
   - Cons: higher ops complexity for pool sizing & autoscaling policy; need routing policy testing.

3) Private Edge Slice + Central Control Plane (privacy-first / sovereign)
   - Pattern: customer-managed edge slice (VPC-hosted inference nodes in EU region) with Redwood control plane for model rollout + metrics. Edge slice handles all EU traffic. NA traffic uses hosted/dedicated as above.
   - Pros: satisfies data residency; gives control for compliance audits; can be air-gapped for future PCI requirements.
   - Cons: procurement + network setup time; on-call / basic infra responsibilities for customer; lower overall utilization unless carefully multiplexed.

Operational considerations and optimizations (tie back to Redwood platform features):
- Batching vs latency: Continuous batching improves cost but increases p95. For checkout flows we recommend explicit per-route config: 1) immediate single-request path with small batch size (2-4 tokens) and strict SLO; 2) asynchronous suggestion path with higher batching.
- KV / prefix caching: for product Q&A, prefix caching of catalog embeddings + KV cache for repeated sessions reduces token counts drastically. Plan: prototype prefix cache on dedicated pool during pilot (measurable decision point).
- Quantization profile: use Redwood Optimize suggestion to run quick eval on customer's prompt set to recommend int8 vs int4 tradeoffs. Include quality regression alert thresholds.
- Smart routing policy: implement canary-first then weighted rollout (10/30/60) with auto-fallback to hosted when 90% of dedicated capacity is reached.
- Network topology: ensure EU edge slice is fronted by local regional LB (no cross-border egress during inference). Document firewall and peering checklist.

SLO-to-cost mapping (back-of-envelope):
- Hosted baseline: p99 120ms -> estimated cost ~ $0.025 / request (depends on model & batch). Pilot monthly at 1M reqs -> ~$25k.
- Dedicated pool (8xA100 equivalent) committed -> $Xk/mo (sizing exercise needed). Breaking point around sustained 300-400 qps.
- Hybrid: reserving dedicated for 150 qps critical routes and overflow to hosted reduces unpredictable spike costs and keeps critical SLAs tight.

Risk matrix (high level):
- Data residency breach risk: Mitigation -> edge slice + strict egress rules; run SOC/pen-testing as add-on.
- Model quality regression at quantization: Mitigation -> pre-release eval sets + rollback rule via Redwood Console.
- Cost overrun in hosted during holiday spikes: Mitigation -> burst caps and automated routing to Dedicated when thresholds hit.
- Operational complexity for Private: Mitigation -> initial managed service engagement and onboarding playbook.

Migration/rollout plan (6–10 week pilot to production ramp):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff + confirm EU data path and compliance owners.
- Week 2: Deploy hosted baseline, collect baseline latencies, run Redwood Optimize eval on sample prompts.
- Week 3–4: Stand up Dedicated pool (minimal size for critical lanes), implement route separation (checkout vs suggestions).
- Week 5: Canary traffic (5% -> 20%) to Dedicated, run quality monitoring and cost telemetry.
- Week 6–8: Increase committed capacity / negotiate contract; start private edge slice planning if customer requires.

Operational runbook (checklist highlights):
- Pre-launch: Sizing test harness, synthetic load to confirm p99 < 110ms on critical path; EV tests for prefix cache hit scenarios.
- Monitoring: Redwood Console alerts for p99 breach, token-level cost spikes, model regression alerts tied to prompt tests.
- Fallback: traffic-shift playbook to divert to hosted region-specific cluster + throttling rules.
- Incident: pre-authorized failover to small-model fast variant with explicit customer notice template.

Open questions / decisions for next customer workshop:
- Exact committed qps for Dedicated reservation (customer provided a 600 qps peak number but not committed floor). Need finance to model committed spend tiers.
- Legal acceptance of control-plane telemetry for Private edge slice (what telemetry can we collect?).
- Does customer accept a small-model fallback for p99 degradation (quality vs latency tradeoff)?
- Appetite for Managed Private deployment vs self-managed (cost split).

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: run Redwood Optimize sample evaluation using customer prompt corpus by 2024-11-22 (deliverable: quantization recommendation + perf table).
- Miguel: draft dedicated pool sizing scenarios and cost model (3 commit tiers) by 2024-11-25.
- Liang: write edge peering & firewall checklist for EU slice and share with customer network team 2024-11-20.
- Emma: create canary rollback runbook + Slack incident template by 2024-11-18.

Appendix (quick experiment ideas to reduce pilot risk):
- Warm pool priming: warm Top-10 prompt prefixes overnight to raise cold-start hit ratio.
- Local suggestion cache: client-side TTL cache for repeated question patterns to reduce backend qps.
- Light-weight reranker hybrid: run a cheap Distil model locally for first-pass and only invoke heavy model on top-k candidates.

Notes to self / friction items observed in workshop:
- Customer wants a single SLA for the whole product — we must clearly document that SLA will be scoped to "critical routes" only.
- Legal asked about auditability of model weights used; propose a model manifest artifact stored per rollout.

Next meeting: schedule with OrbitMall network + compliance (proposed 2024-11-20).

---
Informal collaborators: Miguel (notes on sizing), Liang (network), Emma (runbooks). Treat this doc as the working single source during pilot planning.
